Subject-Level Inference for a Design-MFA Effect

Source: R/design_mfa_inference.R
infer_design_mfa.Rd

Resamples subjects as intact clusters for bootstrap uncertainty. Permutation inference is available only when the caller supplies an explicit `exchangeability` callback; there is deliberately no generic trial shuffle.

Bootstrap loading bases are Procrustes-aligned to the fitted reference basis. Nearly tied components should be interpreted through the returned subspace distances rather than voxelwise loading intervals.

Usage

infer_design_mfa(
  x,
  term,
  method = c("bootstrap", "permutation"),
  statistics = NULL,
  nrep = 200L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  seed = NULL,
  exchangeability = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  use_future = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted [design_mfa()] object.

term

One estimable design term.

method

`"bootstrap"` or `"permutation"`.

statistics

Summaries to compute. The method-dependent default is `c("partial_ss", "singular_values", "subspace")` for the bootstrap and `c("partial_ss", "singular_values")` for permutation inference. Loading intervals are optional because they can be large.

nrep

Number of resampling replicates.

alpha

Total error probability for central percentile intervals.

seed

Optional random seed. The caller's global random-number state is restored on successful and error exits.

exchangeability

For permutation, a function accepting `data`, `term`, and `replicate` and returning a complete refit-data list. The callback owns the scientific validity of the null transformation. Return aligned named `Y`, `design`, `trial_weights`, `block_weight`, `reference_grid`, and `reference_weight` fields (plus `feature_map` for soft alignment). Preserve the frozen reference grid and weights. Malformed refits are failures.

verbose

Emit per-replicate progress. Failed replicates always warn.

use_future

If `TRUE` and the multifer path is unavailable, run independent native refits with [furrr::future_map()]. Multifer permutation and bootstrap stay sequential.

...

Unused.

Value

A `design_mfa_inference` object containing observed statistics, replicate values, failures, and bootstrap summaries or a permutation p-value.

Details

The target is conditional on the fitted reference grid, its cell weights, feature maps, contrasts and chosen penalties/rank. Subject resampling keeps each subject's trials, design and trial weights together and preserves the fitted reference grid/weights; it does not estimate a new population grid. Exchangeability of subjects or a caller-specified null transformation is a scientific assumption, not established by callback schema validation. No unconditional rejection-rate or interval-coverage calibration is claimed.

Bootstrap percentile intervals on `partial_ss` (and other nonnegative statistics) have a positive null expectation and must not be read as a hypothesis test. Use permutation with an explicit `exchangeability` callback to test a term.

Permutation p-values use successful replicates only: `(1 + b) / (n_success + 1)`. Failed refits are not treated as null draws. If `n_success < nrep`, the resolution is `1 / (n_success + 1)` and a warning is issued.

When a multifer build with `effect_significance` is available, serial permutation calls `multifer::infer()`. When the statistic-stability sidecar is also available, bootstrap calls `multifer::bootstrap_fits()` and maps percentile intervals from that sidecar. `use_future = TRUE` no longer starts a local `furrr` loop on those paths.

Examples

# \donttest{
example_data <- design_mfa_example_data()
example_fit <- design_mfa(example_data$Y, example_data$design, ~ saliency)
uncertainty <- infer_design_mfa(
  example_fit, "saliency", statistics = "partial_ss",
  nrep = 5, seed = 10
)
uncertainty$summary$partial_ss
#>   component      label observed    mean          sd    lower    upper
#> 1         1 partial_ss 6.857792 6.85631 0.003164841 6.852106 6.859263
# }
